newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gaz de France seeks strong growth abroad.
newsitem.headline: Gaz de France seeks strong growth abroad.

text.p: Gaz de France (GDF), the French state-owned natural gas group, wants to become a leading energy group by developing abroad, its chairman Pierre Gadonneix told a news conference.
This aim takes account of the strong growth in the use of natural gas and as well of the the ongoing restructuring of the sector where operators are getting bigger and competition gets thougher.
"Faced with this challenge, Gaz de France will respond by growing in France and abroad," Gadonneix said.
In France, GDF wants to increase sales by three percent, more than the market average, by extending its network.
Abroad, Gaz de France is going to extend cooperation deals like the one concluded with Elf-Aquitaine concerning North Sea exploration.

"GDF will become shareholder in field development activities done by joint ventures with Elf Aquitaine," Gadonneix said, adding GDF would buy the gas produced by Elf at market prices. This will involve some two to three billion cubic metres.
Gadonneix said GdF wanted to develop relationships with "natural" partners among which Electricite de France and Total.
"With Total, we are looking at a cooperation project. We hope to be able to conclude a frame-work agreement, like with Elf, soon," he said.
GDF has also signed an industrial partnership with Hydro-Quebec under which the Canadian company will take a 46.4 percent stake in Noverco of the U.S.
GDF will sell six percent of its 24 percent stake.
There are also talks about strengthening GDF's stake in Novergaz, in which GDF now has 30 percent while Hydro-Quebec has 70 percent.
